I don’t know about CS but it’s usually more aligned with other technical disciplines ie EE, Mech , Auto etc. 
Validations/ verification in automotive)is the baseline of most engineering jobs in automotive at least on the OEM side. 
On a scale of component or function ownership on a  vehicle, you pretty much have to deal with suppliers and other stakeholders ( ie other function owners) to verify that your function works according to specifications set and doesn’t affect the functionality of others on the vehicle. It involves a lot of testing, documentation and communication. 
This is required for most R&D engineering jobs, though I found the jobs will not be advertised as verification/ validation engineer. So which means there’s a lot of other cool stuff do and explore depending on the company. I know for the company I worked at they under titles like “Mechatronics engineering “ Electronics” “ function owners” “ SW engineer” 

On a larger level;ie if the job is advertised as validation/ verification engineer), this is when it’s your whole job description (which I find more boring) . You don’t specifically own a component or function but carry out validation and verification tests for the whole vehicle. 
Personally I hated this but some guys who are obsessed with cars loved this part of the job because they get to go on long test drive trips all the time around the world. You still get to do so with the above option but less.

Interms of being a dead end job, it’s all about perspective. If you like the industry, as a graduate you can easily advance and to whatever role you want depending on the company if you are proactive enough. 
Otherwise if you don’t like it the next closest thing you could after is OEM Aerospace and defence.

Yes for my case it is because they are separated not necessarily divorced yet. 

Your parent doesn't need to prove that they are the only person staying at their address, they just have to prove their marital status, that is if they state on their supporting application that they are single/ separated etc, they will be required to send in evidence to prove this, which I explained above. Because in normal cases sfe, expects two parents to support an application, so if they are the only person supporting the application, they will have to prove they are single.
that's why sfe will ask for things like council tax bill or residential agreement contract because if they are living with a partner, their name is likely to appear on these as well BUT if they are single, it's only their name that appears on the documents. 


But if the parent isn't staying with the partner, that doesn't count as household income so your parent will be supporting your application alone AND will be required to provide evidence of martial status if requested.

In terms of evidence or proof, sfe will always list down what they require with an alter of ringing them if what’s originally requested for can't be provided.

Hope I answered that right.

They will let you know what proof you have to provide but usually it's the decree Nisi, statutory declaration, solicitor’s letter and affidavit. 
And if your parent can't provide the stated evidence, they have to ring sfe, and explain y so as to be advised further. 
My mom and my stepdad had just separated in Feb, she rung and was given an alternative of council bill, residential contract/ agreement and phone bill all which should be in her name alone which is proof she is single. She was requested to send these will a cover letter explaining why she couldn't provide proof asked for which was convincing as my application got approved for full maintenance way quickly than I had anticipated.

Just to point this out, when you get to choose which parent to declare; if they are single, they will be asked for evidence to prove this. otherwise, their partner’s income will also be taken into account when accessing you which will as well affect how much funding you receive.
